record.context_brief: binomial width bound for higher local Betti numbers
record.original_question: Let Gamma be a numerical semigroup. For each homological degree i > 1, is the i-th Betti number of the local semigroup ring R_Gamma always bounded above by binom(width(Gamma)+1, i+1)?

evidence.quote: Problem 13 ([CMS23, Conjecture 1.3]). Let Γ be a numerical semigroup, then bi(RΓ ) 6 ( width(Γ)+1 i+1 ) for all i > 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a subset $\Gamma \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ that is closed under addition, contains $0$, and has finite complement in $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. Let $G(\Gamma) = \{n_1 < n_2 < \cdots < n_e\}$ denote the unique minimal system of generators of $\Gamma$, and define the width of $\Gamma$ by
$$\mathrm{width}(\Gamma) = n_e - n_1.$$
Fix a field $k$ and consider the local numerical semigroup ring
$$R_\Gamma = k[\![t^{n_1}, t^{n_2}, \ldots, t^{n_e}]\!] \subseteq k[\![t]\!].$$
Viewing $R_\Gamma$ as a quotient of the local polynomial ring $S = k[\![x_1, \ldots, x_e]\!]$ via $x_j \mapsto t^{n_j}$, let $b_i(R_\Gamma) = \dim_k \mathrm{Tor}_i^S(R_\Gamma, k)$ denote the $i$-th Betti number of $R_\Gamma$.

Question: Is it true that for every numerical semigroup $\Gamma$ and every integer $i > 1$,
$$b_i(R_\Gamma) \;\leq\; \binom{\mathrm{width}(\Gamma) + 1}{i+1}\,?$$
artifact.category_tag: Betti numbers of numerical semigroup rings
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (that Betti numbers of a numerical semigroup ring are bounded by binomial coefficients in the width) appears in recent literature as an open conjecture. Related results bound Betti numbers in terms of the width (Vu; Herzog–others) and verify a conjectural upper bound on the number of defining equations in special cases, but no full proof for all homological degrees $i>1$ was found.

status_evidence.title: Minimal free resolutions of numerical semigroup algebras
status_evidence.snippet: A recent result of Vu shows that if we bound the width of the semigroup, then the Betti numbers of K[H] are bounded; a conjectured upper bound is provided and verified in some cases.
status_evidence.claim: The width-based binomial bound on Betti numbers of numerical semigroup rings is stated as a conjecture and verified only in special cases.

status_evidence.title: Betti numbers for numerical semigroup rings
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of bounds on Betti numbers of numerical semigroup rings.
status_evidence.claim: Bounds on Betti numbers via width are an active area, with the precise binomial bound remaining conjectural.
